mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the economy, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declines > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a potential monetary policy mismatch, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong labor market conditions, which is positive for consumer spending and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in real final sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS declines > 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is increasing and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is decreasing, it suggests a healthy economy with balanced supply and demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM.
